title: Infinite Non-Transient Retry Loop (Thread Hammering)
pattern: A retry loop that retries an operation immediately and indefinitely upon failure, without checking if the failure is transient or permanent, and without backing off.
why_bad: Thread lockup and self-denial of service. Hammering a database or remote API with a bad credential or malformed payload consumes 100% CPU, locks up the calling thread, and logs massive traces that fill disks and overwhelm servers. [7, Chapter 7, "Stubborn Link"]
detection: A recursive or looping construct that retries a fallible operation on every `Err` without an exponential backoff timer, error classification (transient vs. permanent), or a maximum retry count.
source: *Alex Petrov - Database Internals*, Chapter 7 (Stubborn Link Retries) [7]
